errors.text: The proposed critical threshold of 450–500 K is incompatible with the target transition at approximately 900 K; the target remains mechanically stable through 600 K.

The stacking-fault-energy argument is physically inconsistent: high SFE generally disfavors stable extended stacking faults and facilitates cross-slip, whereas low SFE stabilizes partial dislocations and stacking faults and tends to inhibit cross-slip.
The hypothesis predicts stacking-fault annihilation with temperature, while the target reports an increasing HCP atom fraction alongside reduced dislocation line density and rapid lattice disorder.
The proposed validation range ends at 600 K, so it cannot observe or discriminate the actual 900 K transition.
The claimed greater-than-50-percent wear-rate increase and the 450–500 K threshold are not supported by the cited evidence.
